liang2021fine: Fine-grained urban flow prediction must model per-grid transitions across a whole city and separate external factors such as weather for thousands of cells, which coarse-grained methods avoid. STRN uses a backbone to encode each grid, a Global Relation Module that captures global spatial dependencies far more efficiently than prior methods, and a meta learner that turns external factors and land functions such as POI density into meta-knowledge to boost prediction. On two real-world datasets it cuts error by 7.1 to 11.5 percent over the state of the art with fewer parameters and is deployed in the UrbanFlow 3.0 cloud system.
liang2021modeling: RNNs model trajectories in discrete time and update only when a new point arrives, which fits poorly with continuous-time movement, and deterministic RNNs are fragile to sensor noise. TrajODE combines the continuous-time dynamics of neural ordinary differential equations with a stochastic latent space that tolerates observation noise. On trajectory classification it outperforms RNN baselines, showing that continuous-time latent dynamics fit mobility data better than discrete sequence models.
liang2021revisiting: Raster CNNs dominate citywide crowd-flow analysis but learn global spatial dependencies inefficiently and ignore that regions have different latent functions. DeepLGR adds a local feature extractor per region, a global context module that computes global priors and upsamples them to the grid, and a tensor-decomposition region-specific predictor that customizes outputs per region with few parameters. On standard crowd-flow tasks it is more effective, stable, and general than prior CNN models, and the design extends across multiple analytics tasks.
liang2022mixed: Graph convolutional RNNs forecast spatio-temporal city data with pairwise adjacency, but real spatial relations are often higher order across several nodes, and physical laws underlying the data are ignored. MixRNN+ introduces a Mixer block that captures mixed-order spatial relations and a residual update strategy that embeds known and unknown physical constraints. Across traffic speed, taxi flow, and air-quality forecasting it beats state-of-the-art baselines, and a cloud system deploys it as the foundation for smart-city forecasting.
liang2023airformer: Air-quality forecasting over thousands of stations is a large-scale spatio-temporal problem with inherent uncertainty. AirFormer decouples prediction into a bottom-up deterministic stage with two new attention mechanisms that learn spatio-temporal representations efficiently, and a top-down stochastic stage with latent variables that models uncertainty. Trained and evaluated on four years of data from 1,085 stations across mainland China, it reduces 72-hour forecast error by 5 to 8 percent over the previous best model while covering unprecedented spatial granularity.
liu2020active: Labeled nodes are expensive in graph node classification, but active learning usually ignores the representation power of unlabeled nodes. LSCALE uses K-Medoids clustering in a latent space built by dynamically combining unsupervised and supervised features to pick which nodes to label, so that unlabeled structure informs selection. An incremental clustering module prevents redundant choices across labeling rounds. On five datasets it consistently outperforms state-of-the-art graph active learning methods, showing that unlabeled nodes provide useful additional learning signal under a fixed labeling budget.
liu2021eignn: Finite-layer GNNs struggle to capture very long-range graph dependencies. EIGNN is an infinite-depth GNN whose closed-form equilibrium solution makes infinite-depth training tractable, and eigendecomposition further speeds computation. On synthetic and real graphs it captures long-range dependencies better than recent baselines, reaches state-of-the-art node classification, and is more robust to feature noise and adversarial perturbations, showing that infinite-depth message passing can be both expressive and efficient.
liu2022dangling: Knowledge graphs built independently contain dangling entities with no counterpart elsewhere, but conventional entity alignment ignores them. The framework uses local high-order proximity within a nearest-neighbor subgraph and global high-order proximity in the embedding space, jointly for dangling detection and entity matching. Under two evaluation settings it detects dangling entities more precisely and aligns matchable entities better, and further analysis shows it mitigates the hubness problem that plagues dangling-aware alignment.
liu2022lscale: Active learning for node classification picks nodes to label under a budget, yet prior methods learn representations only from labeled nodes and waste unlabeled structure. LSCALE clusters a latent space formed by dynamically mixing unsupervised and supervised features with K-Medoids to select informative nodes, and adds an incremental clustering module that avoids choosing similar nodes across rounds. On five graph datasets it beats state-of-the-art active learning methods by a large margin, confirming that unlabeled node representations carry signal that improves label efficiency.
liu2025unitst: Multivariate time-series forecasting models usually capture variate and temporal dependencies through separate sequential or parallel attention blocks, which cannot explicitly model how series interact within themselves and with each other. UniTST applies one unified attention over flattened patch tokens so that inter-series and intra-series dependencies are learned directly and jointly, with a dispatcher module cutting complexity so the model scales to many variates. Despite its simplicity, it outperforms more complex transformer forecasters on several benchmark datasets.
luo2024fast: Sharpness-aware minimization improves generalization by finding flat minima, but its two forward-backward steps double training cost, a problem for GNNs under few-shot node classification. FGSAM uses a GNN only to compute the weight perturbation and an MLP to minimize the perturbed loss, reusing the perturbation gradient to inject graph topology into the update at almost no extra cost; FGSAM+ applies exact perturbations periodically. With lower compute it beats standard SAM on few-shot node classification, often optimizes faster than the base Adam, and stays competitive on heterophilic node classification.
